mainEntity.name: Does a wood fence actually deter burglars?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partly, and it is worth being precise. In offender interviews, physical barriers rated as the strongest deterrent — stronger than cameras or alarms — and 60% of convicted burglars said they would pick another target if security measures were present. But 65% of residential entries go through doors a fence does not protect. A fence buys time and denies reconnaissance. It is not a burglary solution by itself.

mainEntity.name: What percentage of burglars enter through the back door?

acceptedAnswer.text: 22% of residential burglaries enter through a back door, against 34% at the front door, 23% through first-floor windows, and 9% through the garage door. A backyard fence protects the yard and the route to the back door — the second most common entry point — while leaving the front door untouched.

mainEntity.name: Is a six-foot fence enough to stop someone climbing in?

acceptedAnswer.text: It stops casual climbing, but six feet is not a wall. Most Oakland County residential districts cap side and rear fencing at six feet anyway, so the practical answer is different: remove toe holds, keep nothing climbable beside the line, and make the gate the difficult part of the fence instead of the panel.

mainEntity.name: What is the weakest point of a backyard fence?

acceptedAnswer.text: The gate, nine times out of ten. It is the only moving part, it carries the most load per post, and standard hinges let the leaf be lifted straight off. Anti-lift hinges, a padlockable latch mounted above reach, and a drop rod on double gates close the biggest gap in a residential fence.

mainEntity.name: Do fence spikes stop burglars, and are they legal?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are a liability problem more than a security measure. Spikes, broken glass set into a top rail, and anti-climb paint create injury exposure, can conflict with local code and HOA rules, and are defeated by a jacket laid over the top. We do not install them and do not recommend them on residential fencing in a subdivision.

mainEntity.name: Does a solid privacy fence make a house easier to break into?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can. A solid six-foot panel blocks sight lines in both directions, which means it also hides someone working in your yard from neighbours and from the street. The fix is deliberate design: solid where you need privacy, open or camera-covered where you need visibility, and lighting aimed into the yard rather than at the fence.

mainEntity.name: Does a fence lower homeowners insurance in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not as a line item. Carriers commonly credit monitored alarm systems and deadbolts, not fences. What a fence does reliably is support an underwriting or claims conversation — photograph the finished fence and gate hardware and keep the receipt so the improvement is on record.

mainEntity.name: What is the best gate lock for a wooden fence?

acceptedAnswer.text: A padlockable latch or cane bolt mounted high on the inside, paired with anti-lift hinges and a gate stop. Keyed-alike locks mean one key serves house and gate. But the lock matters less than what it is bolted to: a latch on a sagging gate is decoration.

mainEntity.name: How do I stop my gate being lifted off its hinges?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replace standard hinges with anti-lift or security hinges that have a fixed or non-removable pin, or add a hinge-side security plate. On a double gate, a drop rod into a ground receiver closes the other half of the opening. On most residential gates it is a two-hour retrofit.

mainEntity.name: When should I check my fence for security gaps in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before daylight saving time ends on November 1, when Detroit sunset moves from 6:29 PM to 5:27 PM in a single weekend. Walk the perimeter with a flashlight after dark, test the gate with gloves on, clear any snow-ramp launch point before the first plow, and confirm exterior lights and timers actually fire.
